techniques.name: SCAMPER-Substitute
techniques.def: Swap one element (material, physics, carrier, substrate, signal, tool) for something different.

techniques.name: SCAMPER-Combine
techniques.def: Fuse two existing technologies/functions into one structure or system.

techniques.name: SCAMPER-Adapt
techniques.def: Borrow a solution that already works in another industry and adapt it.

techniques.name: SCAMPER-Magnify/Minify
techniques.def: Make something drastically bigger, smaller, faster, slower, more or fewer.

techniques.name: SCAMPER-Eliminate
techniques.def: Remove a part everyone assumes is required (capacitor, refresh, EUV, periphery, binary...).

techniques.name: SCAMPER-Reverse/Rearrange
techniques.def: Flip the order, direction, roles or layout (read/write, array/periphery, memory/compute).

techniques.name: TRIZ inventive principles
techniques.def: Apply TRIZ's 40 principles (segmentation, nesting, asymmetry, prior action, dynamics, periodic action, phase transition, self-service, etc.) and resolve a contradiction such as 'smaller cell but more charge'.

techniques.name: Biomimicry
techniques.def: Copy how nature stores and retrieves information or energy (synapses, DNA, immune memory, ion channels, plants, slime mould, magnetotactic bacteria, chromatophores).

techniques.name: Cross-domain analogy
techniques.def: Map a working idea from another field (batteries, displays, solar, MEMS, optics, HDDs, vinyl, logistics, finance, cities, cooking).

techniques.name: Forgotten-technology revival
techniques.def: Revive and modernize abandoned memory tech (core, Williams tube, delay line, bubble, twistor, plated wire, early FeRAM, drum) with 2026 tools.

techniques.name: Assumption inversion
techniques.def: List DRAM's hidden assumptions (charge storage, separate from compute, must be perfect, binary, uniform cells, 2D, silicon, synchronous, refreshed) and invert one.

techniques.name: First principles
techniques.def: Derive from physical minima (kT, charge quanta, leakage physics, energy per bit moved) and rebuild from scratch.

techniques.name: Random stimulus / forced connection
techniques.def: Pick unrelated random objects or words and force a connection to memory.

techniques.name: Morphological box (Zwicky)
techniques.def: Combine one option per axis (storage medium x access device x sensing x integration x substrate x fab method) into non-obvious combinations.

techniques.name: Provocation (de Bono 'Po')
techniques.def: Start from an absurd statement ('Po: memory that forgets on purpose', 'Po: chips grown not made') and extract a workable idea.

techniques.name: Reverse brainstorming
techniques.def: Ask how to make the RAM crisis WORSE, then flip each answer.

techniques.name: Perspective shift / personas
techniques.def: Think as a child, an alien, a 2050 engineer, a Soviet engineer under embargo, a farmer, an artist, or a biologist.

techniques.name: Extreme users and edge cases
techniques.def: Design for extremes (space, cryo, 200C downhole, AI KV-cache, $1 IoT, 30-year industrial) and see what generalizes.

techniques.name: Scale and time shifting
techniques.def: Jump across scales (molecule to wafer to rack to datacenter) and timescales (ns to s to years of retention).

techniques.name: Failure mining
techniques.def: Take a failed memory venture or tech (Optane, Z-RAM, T-RAM, bubble memory, Nantero, HPE memristor) and fix exactly what killed it.

techniques.name: Physical-effects walk
techniques.def: Walk through physics phenomena (piezo, pyro, magnetostriction, Mott transition, Coulomb blockade, tunneling, spin Hall, electrochromism, photoconductivity, ion migration, thermal hysteresis) and turn each into a storage or sensing mechanism.

techniques.name: Periodic-table walk
techniques.def: Go element by element, favoring abundant ones (Si, Al, Ti, Fe, Zn, Sn, C, N, O, Na, Mg, Ca, S), and ask what each could do in memory.

techniques.name: Manufacturing analogies
techniques.def: Borrow fabrication methods (printing press, roll-to-roll, 3D printing, weaving, origami, self-assembly, crystal growth, casting, fermentation).

techniques.name: Wishful thinking / ideal final result
techniques.def: Describe the ideal memory ('free, infinite, instant, zero energy') and work backward to what is closest to achievable.

techniques.name: Scarcity and constraint as engine
techniques.def: Necessity breeds ingenuity: impose a harsh limit and invent within it (fill every idea with the cell's forced constraint).

facets.name: Bit storage element
facets.def: How the bit is physically held (charge, polarization, spin, phase, ions, mechanics, light...).

facets.name: Access device, leakage and refresh
facets.def: The switch that isolates the bit; retention; refresh energy and time.

facets.name: Sensing and periphery
facets.def: Reading tiny signals; sense amps, decoders, the ~49% of die area that is periphery.

facets.name: Array architecture and 3D integration
facets.def: Cell layout, 4F2, vertical/stacked arrays, bonding, layer count.

facets.name: Materials and resource intensity
facets.def: Scarce or concentrated inputs (helium, quartz, tungsten, hafnium, PFAS), energy, water, abundant substitutes.

facets.name: Manufacturing, lithography and capital intensity
facets.def: Process steps, masks, EUV dependence, tool cost, fab cost, throughput.

facets.name: System architecture: need less DRAM
facets.def: Compression, dedup, tiering, compute-in-memory, data placement, approximate memory, KV-cache tricks.

facets.name: Interface, packaging and data movement
facets.def: HBM, TSVs, interposers, pJ/bit, optical or wireless links, chiplets.

facets.name: Reliability, ECC and error tolerance
facets.def: Making weaker or cheaper cells acceptable; row hammer; retention tails; self-healing.

facets.name: Supply, industry and strategy
facets.def: New ways to raise usable memory supply: reuse/recycling, micro-fabs, open IP, cooperatives, financing, policy, distributed manufacturing, business models.

constraints: No helium, neon or other rare gases
Only Earth-abundant elements (no Hf, Ru, Co, W, Ta, In, Ga)
Must be buildable in a university nanofab
No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity
Must reach 10x density at the same cost
Must be made entirely in the U.S.
Must work with today's DDR/HBM interfaces unchanged
Must be manufacturable by a 10-person team
Must tolerate 1% bit error rate at the cell
Must be 100x cheaper per GB, any other trade-off allowed
